hints: Look closely at the two C=O groups on the ring and ask whether the carbonyl carbon is joined to a hydrogen or to two carbons.
Remember that each double bond contains exactly one pi bond, so start by counting the two C=O and the two C=C bonds in the six-membered ring.
Add the one C=C in each repeating side-chain unit to your ring total to get the full expression in terms of n.
walkthrough:
**Decide aldehyde or ketone**

Look at the two $C=O$ groups on the ring. Each carbonyl carbon is part of the ring and bonded to two other ring carbons, with no $C-H$ on that carbon.

Rule: $R-CHO$ (with H) is an aldehyde, $R-CO-R'$ is a ketone. So this is a diketone, in fact a quinone, not an aldehyde.

**Count pi bonds in the ring**

Each double bond has one $\sigma$ bond plus one $\pi$ bond. So count double bonds.

In the ring: $$2 \times C=O \text{ gives } 2 \text{ } \pi \text{ bonds}$$
$$2 \times C=C \text{ gives } 2 \text{ } \pi \text{ bonds}$$
Ring total = 4 pi bonds.

**Count pi bonds in the side chain**

The bracketed repeat unit shows: $-CH_2-CH=C(CH_3)-CH_2-$. That contains one $C=C$ per repeat.

$$1 \text{ repeat } = 1 \times \pi \text{ bond}$$
$$n \text{ repeats } = n \times \pi \text{ bonds}$$

**Combine for the total**

Add ring and chain together.

$$\text{total } \pi = 4 + n = n+4$$
So the coenzyme is a ketone with $n+4$ pi bonds in one molecule.

options.A: Incorrect. It is not an aldehyde because the C=O carbons have no hydrogen attached, they are bonded to two ring carbons. The count n+2 also misses two pi bonds from the ring.
options.B: Incorrect. The pi count n+4 is right, but the functional group is wrong. Students choosing this have counted correctly but mistaken any C=O for an aldehyde, forgetting the aldehyde needs a -CHO hydrogen.
options.C: Incorrect. Ketone is correct, but n+2 is too low. This usually comes from counting only one ring C=C plus the two C=O, or forgetting that the quinone ring has two C=C double bonds.
options.D: Correct. Both C=O groups are ketonic (cyclic diketone) and total pi bonds are 2 from C=O + 2 from ring C=C + n from the side-chain C=C, giving n+4.
